seoTitle: Obstacles & Soil Load: 5 Factors Raising Blind & Shade Cleaning Quotes
metaDescription: Obstacles, soil load, escorts, and access height can push blind ultrasonic and shade cleaning quotes up 15%-45%. See the math, then compare bids in our tool.
excerpt: Two offices with the same number of blinds can receive ultrasonic cleaning quotes that differ by 40%. This guide breaks down the five site conditions estimators price in, how much each adds, and what you can do before the walkthrough to keep your bid near the base rate.
quickAnswer: Ultrasonic blind and roller shade cleaning quotes typically start around $10-$18 per horizontal blind and $15-$35 per roller shade, then rise 15%-45% when estimators see furniture obstacles, heavy soil load, after-hours security escorts, high or hard-to-reach mounting, or delicate and motorized shades. Clearing window lines, sharing soil history, and scheduling during normal access hours are the fastest ways to pull a quote back toward base pricing.

blocks.text: Why identical blind counts produce very different bids

Window-covering estimators start from a unit price, but they bid labor minutes. A standard 36 x 60 in aluminum blind takes a two-person crew about 6-10 minutes to remove, tank, rinse, dry, and re-hang when the window line is clear and the soil is ordinary office dust. Every condition that adds minutes per unit, or adds non-productive hours to the night, gets priced in. At specialty labor rates of $55-$95 per technician hour, an extra four minutes per blind across 80 blinds adds $290-$500 to a project before any markup.

The five factors below account for nearly all of the 15%-45% variance we see between base quotes and final bids on office projects. Some are fixed features of your building; others you can fix before the estimator ever walks the floor.

Credenzas, filing cabinets, planters, standing desks, and monitor arms parked against the glass are the most common upcharge. Technicians cannot safely lift a blind off its brackets while leaning over a desk, and most vendors will not move IT equipment at all for liability reasons. Expect a 10%-20% uplift or a per-window obstacle fee of $3-$8 if more than a quarter of window lines are blocked. Some vendors instead bill furniture moving at standard janitorial rates of $35-$65 per hour, which is often cheaper if you have only a few blocked rooms.
Factor 2: Soil load and residue type

Ordinary dust lifts in one tank cycle. Cooking grease near breakrooms, nicotine film in older buildings, toner haze near print rooms, and fine drywall dust after a renovation can require a second cycle, a stronger alkaline degreaser with longer dwell time, or hand-detailing of ladder cords. Heavy soil commonly adds 15%-30% to affected units. Roller shades with UV-baked grime on the glass side may need spot treatment that lengthens drying time before re-hang.

blocks.title: Typical uplift ranges by factor
blocks.text: Obstacles and furniture moving: +10% to +20%. Heavy soil load: +15% to +30% on affected units. After-hours escorts: +$45 to +$85 per escort hour or +10% to +15%. Access height over 10 ft: +15% to +25%. Motorized or delicate shades: +$8 to +$20 per unit. Stacked together, a difficult site lands 30%-45% above base.
Factor 3: After-hours security escorts and access windows

Many Class A towers, government-leased floors, law firms, and healthcare offices require a building engineer or security officer to accompany outside vendors after hours. If the escort is billed back to the tenant at $45-$85 per hour, or if the vendor loses productive time waiting for elevators to be keyed and suites to be unlocked, the quote rises. Tight access windows, such as 10 p.m. to 4 a.m. only, also force larger crews to finish on time, raising mobilization cost.
Factor 4: Mounting height and access equipment

Blinds above 10 feet, clerestory shades, and atrium windows need extension ladders, rolling scaffolds, or a scissor lift. That adds setup and teardown time, fall-protection requirements, and sometimes equipment rental. Uplifts of 15%-25% on high units are typical, and lift rental may be billed at cost. Double-height lobbies are the usual culprit, and they are also the most visible coverings in the building.
Factor 5: Delicate, oversized, or motorized coverings

Motorized roller shades must be disconnected, tagged, and tested after re-hang, adding $8-$20 per unit. Oversized horizontals over 60 sq ft may need extra hands. Fabric verticals, sheers, and blackout laminates often cannot go in an ultrasonic tank and require slower hand cleaning. Vendors also price in risk for brittle 15-year-old slats that crack on removal; expect a damage waiver or a per-unit replacement clause.

blocks.text: How to keep your quote close to base

items.name: Clear window lines before the walkthrough
items.text: Ask occupants to move personal items and have facilities relocate furniture the afternoon before. Estimators bid what they see, so a cleared floor at the walkthrough produces a cleaner number.

items.name: Share soil history honestly
items.text: Tell bidders about recent construction, kitchen proximity, or past smoking. A surprise heavy-soil change order on cleaning night costs more than a priced-in uplift.

items.name: Pre-arrange building access
items.text: Coordinate keyed elevators, dock time, and escort schedules with property management in writing. Ask whether a building engineer can be scheduled during regular overtime rather than billed as a special escort.

items.name: Bundle high work
items.text: If you already rent a lift for interior glass or light-fixture cleaning, schedule blind work the same night to share setup cost.

items.name: Separate delicate units
items.text: List motorized and fabric shades as their own line so standard blinds are not priced with a blanket risk premium.

blocks.text: The supporting housekeeping on that same night also matters to your property manager. Crews working near restrooms and breakrooms often top off consumables at the same time: a controlled one-at-a-time roll-towel dispenser with a key lock reduces restock trips, 30-day enzymatic urinal screens keep odor complaints down while doors are propped for equipment, and if the window project coincides with a VCT strip-and-recoat, a stripper and acrylic finish combo keeps the floor schedule on one mobilization.

blocks.title: Risk items to resolve before signing
blocks.text: Confirm the vendor's certificate of insurance covers property damage to window coverings, that technicians on ladders above 6 ft follow a written fall-protection plan, and that Safety Data Sheets for degreasers are on site under OSHA HazCom. Ask for a written damage policy on aged slats and clutches.

Run your blind and shade counts through the Office Cleaning Cost Calculator to set a baseline, then enter each bid's uplifts into the Quote Comparator to see which site factors are driving the difference.

faqs.q: What is a reasonable markup for heavy soil on ultrasonic blind cleaning?
faqs.a: A 15%-30% uplift on the affected units is reasonable for grease, nicotine, toner, or post-construction dust that needs a second tank cycle or longer degreaser dwell time. Be wary of a building-wide soil uplift when only breakroom or print-room zones are heavily soiled; ask for it to be applied by zone.

faqs.q: Can I avoid security escort fees for after-hours blind cleaning?
faqs.a: Sometimes. Ask property management whether the vendor can be added to the approved after-hours contractor list with badge access, or whether the work can happen on a Saturday during engineer coverage. If an escort is unavoidable, get the hourly rate in writing and cap the hours in the work order.

faqs.q: Why do motorized roller shades cost more to clean?
faqs.a: Motorized shades must be powered down, disconnected, labeled, and tested after re-hang, and some require limit resetting. That adds labor and risk, typically $8-$20 per unit above manual shade pricing. Confirm the vendor will not void the shade manufacturer's warranty.

faqs.q: Does the janitorial crew move furniture for blind cleaning?
faqs.a: Not by default. Furniture moving is usually excluded from both the base janitorial scope and the blind vendor's unit price. You can authorize it as an extra at standard janitorial rates of $35-$65 per hour, or have your facilities team clear the window lines in advance.

faqs.q: How should I compare quotes when vendors price site factors differently?
faqs.a: Ask every bidder to separate base unit pricing from each uplift, then total them on an annual basis. Convert annual cost to monthly by dividing by 12, and to weekly by dividing the monthly figure by 4.333, so you can line them up against your janitorial contract structure.
